title: Contemporary metaphysics: grounding, fundamentality and metaontology
stage: Graduate study and research in metaphysics
audience: a philosophy graduate preparing for doctoral study and research in metaphysics, or a graduate student in the first years of a PhD
purpose: Work through current research in metaphysics at the graduate level: metaontology (Quine, Carnap and their successors, quantifier variance and easy ontology), grounding and metaphysical explanation, fundamentality and priority monism, essence and real definition, Humean supervenience and its rivals, powers, metaphysical indeterminacy, and the epistemology of metaphysics, reading research papers and writing seminar papers.
primary_reading: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Metaphysical Grounding (free)

weeks.1: Metaontology: Quine, Carnap and the existence question
weeks.2: Deflationism, quantifier variance and easy ontology
weeks.3: Grounding: the idea and its logic
weeks.4: Skepticism about grounding and its alternatives
weeks.8: Powers, dispositions and the new essentialism
weeks.9: Metaphysical indeterminacy and vagueness in the world
weeks.10: Time and tense in current metaphysics
weeks.11: The epistemology of metaphysics: intuitions, theoretical virtues and naturalism
weeks.12: Writing and presenting a seminar paper

blocks.deliverable: Write a seminar response paper on quantifier variance.
Present the formal properties of grounding with examples.
Reconstruct the argument for priority monism.
Week 7 midterm; write a seminar paper proposal.
Present a recent argument about metaphysical indeterminacy.
Submit a seminar paper draft for review.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Seminar paper: write a 5,000- to 7,000-word seminar paper on one current debate from the course that surveys the literature accurately, reconstructs the main argument, and defends an original objection, reply or refinement; revise it after written feedback and present it in 20 minutes.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
